Skill Amplification is the strongest stat and it looks the weakest

At every rarity and every tier bar the very bottom one, where it ties, Skill Amplification rolls a smaller number than the stats around it. SSR Tier 01 gives 5.00 where CRIT DMG gives 8.00. That gap is the game pricing it, not undervaluing it. It multiplies a skill's whole output rather than its damage alone, buffs included, so it pays even on a Cookie that never hits anything: a test on August 10, 2026 measured a caster's own Skill AMP raising the Skill AMP its buff granted an ally, at 0.60 per point. Do not skip it because the number is small, and do not skip it on a support.

Skill Haste is the rarest line in the game, not the easiest

The thirteen ordinary stats share one probability per tier. Skill Haste has its own, and at the tiers where it appears it is between 1.25 and 2.7 times the shared rate, which is where the "easy to get" reading comes from. But it only appears on four of the twelve tiers: SSR and SR, tiers 01 and 02. It cannot roll on an R, U or C rune at all. Across the whole pool that puts it at 1 in 261 against 1 in 13 for every other stat. It is the one line worth deliberately crafting for, because you will not stumble into it.

A perfect rune is not a plan

The best roll in the game, SSR Tier 01, sits at 0.007663 percent per stat. That is one craft in thirteen thousand, and there are thirteen stats competing for it. Craft for the stat you need and take the tier you are given. Anyone telling you to reroll for SSR Tier 01 has not read the table.

What the disclosure does not say

  • What a craft costs is not in the article. The probabilities are disclosed because Korean law requires probabilities, not prices.
  • Elemental DMG is not in the rune pool at all. It comes from Pets only, so no amount of crafting will produce it.

The developer rounds every published cell, so the column sums to 100 to four decimal places rather than exactly. That is the disclosure as published, not a transcription error. Pool sums to 100%. Article last updated 2026-07-30.

Stage index

Every stage in the campaign, what waits at the end of it, what that boss is carrying, and what the stage pays you while you are logged out. The in-game map shows you one stage at a time, never shows the boss stat line at all, and never shows the reward rate, which is the whole reason this exists.

Enter a stage and it returns the boss, how many spawn, the recommended Power, the Accuracy and Focus the stage demands, the boss health, attack and defense, how many kills open the boss fight, and the offline income the stage pays per hour. Add your own team Power and it also tells you which damage bracket you are standing in and what the next one costs.

Loading the stage tables.

Offline income is a step function, not a curve

Rewards do not rise stage by stage. They hold flat across a band and then jump. Parking one stage below a boundary can cost you a large fraction of your hourly income for no reason at all, so the thing worth checking is not "can I clear this" but "am I sitting just under a step".

Farm the highest stage you have cleared, not the hardest one you can survive

Offline income is paid by the stage you are parked on. Clearing further and then parking further is the entire mechanic, and it is why pushing the campaign beats optimising a team for a wall you cannot pass.

The damage bracket is a ratio, and it is brutal below 10 percent

Under a tenth of the recommended Power you deal 1 percent damage. Reaching a tenth takes you to 5 percent, and the scale climbs from there to 120 percent at 1.2 times recommended. A stage you are far under is not slow, it is arithmetically impossible, and no amount of retrying changes that.

There is no wall at a chapter boundary

Recommended Power never falls and almost never leaps. The largest single step in all 9,839 of them is 1-4 into 1-5, at 1.36 times, and every one of the fifteen biggest sits inside a chapter rather than on its edge. The steepest boundary in the whole game is 1-30 into 2-1 at 1.04 times. If you are stuck, you are stuck on a slot, not on a chapter.

Stage 20 and stage 30 are elite slots, and they hit about three times harder

Both send exactly one body, on all 656 of them, with no exception anywhere in the campaign. Their attack against the recommended Power of the stage they sit in runs about three times what a normal slot in the same chapter carries, on two in three of them, and under double on roughly one in four. The one boss that breaks the pattern is GingerCraven, who closes roughly every fourth chapter and hits closer to a normal slot than an elite. Everywhere else, that is where a run ends, and it is why the boss attack column is worth reading before you park.

Past 168-30 the boss outgrows the gate

From 168-30 to 328-30 the recommended Power asks for 51 times more, and the boss brings 117 times the health for it. Attack grows under 7 times over and Defense barely moves. Meeting the recommended figure in the late chapters buys you less than the same figure bought you earlier, and the shortfall is health, so it costs you time rather than survival.

Enemy Accuracy stops climbing, and nothing tells you

The Accuracy the enemy brings against your Evasion reaches its ceiling at 168-29 and then holds flat for the final 4,802 stages, nearly half the campaign. The Accuracy a stage demands of you keeps climbing for another eighty chapters past that, to 248-28, before it finds a ceiling of its own; Focus never stops rising at all. Evasion gets quietly better the deeper you go. The bars you have to clear do not, and one of them never stops.

The developer publishes no stage table, no boss list, no boss stat line and no offline reward rate. Recommended Power, the boss stat line, the sub-stat requirements and the offline reward rates are read from the stage table inside the game client, for all 9,840 stages. The first 3,000 recommended Power figures were also compiled here stage by stage before any dataset existed, and they agree exactly. Corrected October 4, 2026: recommended Power, boss health and boss attack from 169-1 onward were an extrapolation that ran high, by up to 36 percent on Power at 328-30. They now match the game. Damage brackets are derived from the recommended figure rather than stored, because every threshold reproduces from it alone.

A stage checks three numbers against your squad. The Stage Index answers Power. This answers the two the game never explains, and names which of the three actually stops you, because that is the only one worth spending on.

10-16

328 chapters, 30 stages each, 9,840 in total.

16

Two sliders rather than one, because landing on a single stage out of 9,840 with a thumb is not a control.

150,000

The total on your Lineup screen. Log-scaled, because the campaign runs from 1,600 to just over 2 billion.

100

Baseline is 100. A rate of 1.0 on the enemy side is 100 points on yours.

100

Baseline is 100. Focus decides whether your debuffs and disables land at all.

20%

The number printed on the skill, before Focus touches it. Dark Choco's DEF Down is 20 percent.

Resistance is a dead roll in the campaign. Enemy Avoidance runs 1.0 to 12.04 and enemy Resist 1.0 to 11.62 across the full ladder. Enemy Accuracy climbs to 16.62 by 168-29 and then stops, holding flat for the last 4,801 stages. Enemy Focus never moves off exactly 1.0, and that now reads across all 9,840 stages to 328-30 rather than stopping at 168-30. Focus beats their Resist and matters enormously. Resistance would beat their Focus, and nothing in the campaign pushes against it. Scope that to the campaign: this data covers stages only, and a real opponent in the Arena does bring Focus.

Both are modelled, and both formulas are exact rather than fitted to observed behaviour. Hit chance is Accuracy divided by enemy Avoidance, clamped at 100 percent, and enemy Avoidance is 100 times the stage's Avoidance rate, which is the bar in the table above. Debuff rate is the listed chance multiplied by Focus over enemy Resist. One caveat on the Accuracy bar: it assumes the enemy has the standard base Avoidance of 100, true of 154 of the 166 monsters, while seven elites sit at 50 and need only half of it. Source: community data supplied by a player, the same numbers behind the community tool at kopicsiudai.github.io/crumble. Its Power column agrees with the 3,000 stages this hub compiled itself before any community dataset existed, exactly, which is why the two are treated as corroborating each other. A later export carrying the enemy rate columns themselves reproduces all three bars above on every one of the 9,840 stages, so the 1.0 to 100 scale is now checked end to end rather than over the first 5,040.

Package value

Every bundle in the shop, converted to one unit so they can be compared at all. The store shows you one package at a time and never shows you what the last one was worth, which is how a bad deal survives.

Everything a package contains is priced in Crystals, then divided by what the package costs. A draw ticket is worth the Crystals a draw costs. A guaranteed SSR Cookie is worth the 180 draws the Pick-up guarantee takes, because that is the deterministic price of one. The ranking is what matters, not the raw total: bigger packages contain more of everything, so totals only tell you which one is expensive.

Count only what you need
Shop section

Counting 13 of 13 currencies across 57 packages. Best value is Nameless Cake Hound 3-Star Package at 45.25 Crystals per won, which is 20.1 times the median package.

Ranked, best value first

Value is not the same as worth

A package rated highly here is dense in Crystals per unit spent. It is not necessarily a good purchase. A bundle of Pet draws is worthless if your Pets are already built, and duplicates of a Cookie you cannot use are worth nothing whatever the arithmetic says. Use the toggles to count only what you actually need.

Two of the conversions are arguments, not facts

Crystals per draw is observed and solid. Pricing a guaranteed SSR at 180 draws is a defensible choice rather than a published rate, and an SR Cookie is valued at a single draw because nothing exists to price it against, which understates it. Both are stated here rather than buried so you can disagree with them.

Prices are the Korean store in won

That is the catalogue this was read from. It does not weaken the ranking: every storefront prices the same catalogue proportionally, so which package is best is the same everywhere. Read the ordering, not the won figure.

Stage power chart

Damage in Crumble is a ratio, not a flat number. The stage carries a recommended Power figure, your squad is measured against it, and the game pays out a damage percentage off a fixed scale. This chart is that scale for every stage from 1-1 to 328-30, all 9,840 of them.

The useful part is that the scale is the same everywhere. Every threshold is a fixed fraction of the stage's recommended Power: 10% of it puts you in the 5% damage tier, 20% in 15%, 40% in 35%, 60% in 55%, 80% in 75%, the recommended figure itself is 100%, and 120% of it tops the scale out at 120%. Learn that once and you can read any stage in the game without the table.

Damage lab

EOG's own battle model. Put your gear in once and every Cookie in the game is ranked by what its kit actually does at your investment, against the target you pick. Change a number and the order changes with it.

That is the part a tier list cannot do. Crit is worth little on a kit that fires once every eight seconds and a lot on one that fires every two. Skill Haste and Skill AMP trade almost evenly, because haste buys casts rather than bigger hits. Boss DMG is dead weight outside a boss fight. Tap any row for the arithmetic.

Your gear

ATK multiplier is what level, plating, Sugar Runes and Stellar Link have done to a Cookie's base attack. If you do not know it, divide the ATK on any Cookie's profile by its base figure in the roster.

Target

Coefficient bound

19 of the 76 kits have a shape whose single-target hit count cannot be settled from the data: a fan of projectiles that may or may not all reach one body, a Chain bounce that needs a second body to bounce to. Those carry both ends and are marked on the board. The rest are unaffected by this control.

Every Cookie, ranked at your gear

A stat is not your base plus the sum of your bonuses. The engine folds each source in its own layer, so the same plus twelve percent is worth more in a layer you have not filled yet. Enter your build and this reads the whole assembly back, then puts the result through the per-hit damage equation.

Cookie

Stat sources

Each layer folds in the engine's order. Whether a layer gives a flat amount or a percentage is fixed by the game, and is the same for ATK, DEF and HP.

Arena Fame folds here too but carries no ATK, DEF or HP at all, only CRIT DMG, so it is not listed.

Resolve

The game shows your Resolve Stage and each stat's Level, not the total they add. Enter those and the Resolve line above is worked out for ATK, DEF and HP.

Damage reduction

Enter every source of damage reduction on its own: each equipment piece, your Pet, perks, Sugar Runes and so on. They multiply rather than add, so order makes no difference to the total. Need more than six? Add a source.

    Crumble Dungeon simulator

    Crumble Dungeon gives you no controls at all. Your squad is committed, forty Cookies stand on the field, and everything after that is decided by numbers the game never prints: attack range decides which slot a Cookie is placed in, move speed decides when it arrives, and an arena-wide shockwave throws the whole team backwards four times during the run.

    The boss then buffs its own damage reduction three times. Reduction in this game screens rather than adds, so those buffs compound instead of capping out, and a run is effectively decided in its first thirteen seconds. That is why a damage-per-second ranking of the roster is the wrong ranking for this mode, and it is the ranking everybody publishes. This tool weights damage against the armour curve instead, so a Cookie that arrives late is scored for arriving late.

    Your gear, applied across the lineup

    One profile across the whole lineup, because the base stat block is a fixed template per class and nobody gears Cookies differently in practice. What comes out is a ranking of kits at equal investment, which is the comparison worth having. Attack is not in this row: it comes from the level and grade curves below.

    Investment

    Level and grade both multiply the base stat block, and whether they pool or compound is not settled. At level 100 grade 10 the two readings differ by more than half again, so both are offered and the smaller one leads. Everything in the gear row above is added on top of this.

    What to run

    Turning effects off is the comparison the rest of this hub could not make before: it is what the lineup scores with every heal, shield, buff and debuff removed and nothing but raw damage left. The gap between the two is what your supports are actually worth.

    Slot order

    Attack range ascending is the observed rule, and it is a reading rather than a settled fact. The other two are there so you can see how much the uncertainty is actually worth, which for most lineups is very little.

    Boss armour, and the coefficient bound

    Each boss buff stacks to five and the data states one application per source. Both ends are offered because the accrual rate is not settled. Sixteen kits have a shape whose single-target hit count is not knowable, so those carry a range too.

    What this model does not know

      Battle simulator

      Community tool Crumble Battle Simulator built by mokocoder

      This is the one tool on the hub EOG did not build. mokocoder wrote a working model of Crumble combat, and it is the closest thing the game has to a test server: pick a lineup, pick a fight, and watch it resolve. It runs the whole roster, all 76 Cookies and 57 Pets, against every campaign boss.

      The original ships in Korean. It runs here in English, with Cookies, Pets and bosses named the way the rest of this hub names them, so a fight you scout in the Stage Index is spelled the same when you simulate it. Only the wording changed: every number on screen is the simulator's own, and the original is linked below the frame.

      Boss fights

      Run any of the 38 campaign bosses against a 12-slot lineup and watch the fight play back frame by frame.

      Arena matches

      Put two of your own decks against each other on a fixed seed, from both sides, so neither gets the first-strike advantage for free.

      Stage and Arena evaluation

      Batch dozens of runs per deck and rank the results by clear rate, average score and clear time instead of one lucky pull of the RNG.

      Deck manager

      Build and save lineups with level, star grade, Captain, Pets and Mercenary Band perks. Saved in your browser, not on an account.

      Crumble Battle Simulator, English Open in a tab Original
      Loading the simulator. It pulls its engine and sprites on first open, so give it a moment.

      Before you trust a number

      • It is a model of the fight, not the fight. Treat a result as a strong comparison between two lineups rather than a promise about your next run.
      • Every battle is seeded. Change the seed and the same two decks can trade places, which is exactly why the evaluation modes run a deck dozens of times before ranking it.
      • Decks are saved in your browser only. Clearing site data clears them, and they do not follow you to another device.
      • The roster comes from the simulator, not from this hub. If a Cookie shipped this week and the simulator has not picked it up yet, it will not be selectable here either.
      • A few skill and buff lines inside the battle log still read in Korean. Those sit in the simulator engine rather than its interface, and EOG would rather leave a line untranslated than guess at what an effect does and have you build around the guess.

      With thanks to mokocoder

      The simulator is entirely mokocoder's work, built and made public for free. EOG did the English wording and nothing else. If it saves you a bad 12-Cookie investment, that is down to them: the original lives at crumb.run, and they are reachable on Discord as mokocoder.

      The English is ours, so a translation slip is ours too. Report one in the EOG Discord rather than to mokocoder, and we will fix it on our side.

      All 76 Cookies and all 57 Pets are listed: the 69 Cookies and 54 Pets that launched, Cool Mint Cookie from the August 13 update, and the six Cookies and three Pets added since, read from the 1.4.002 game client. Rarity, element, class and Synergy provision are complete for every Cookie. Skill name, cooldown, effect text and stats are carried for 30 of them: the entire high-rarity pool plus Herb Cookie at SR. The in-game catalogue prints all of it at every rarity down to C, so the other 46 are untranscribed rather than unpublished. Both Pet effect layers are complete.

      Patch 1.4.002 client · updated October 4, 2026

      Skill text for the launch pool is translated from the Japanese version, because that is the only version anyone has written out in full. Two entries are not: Herb Cookie, transcribed off an English card, and Cool Mint Cookie, whose name and card text Devsisters published in English themselves. Names an English-language source also prints are tagged Confirmed, and on the launch pool that tag covers the NAME only: no effect line, number or stat label below it has been read off an English card. Treat a stat name inside a translated line as unverified rather than just differently worded. It has been wrong once already, on Pomegranate Cookie, published here as an ATK buff when the game grants Skill AMP, corrected on August 1, 2026 from a player report. Effect lines describe what the skill does, not how much it does.

      57 Pets: 54 at launch, counted in game as SSR 23, SR 12, R 9, U 6, C 4, and three SSR added since, Chargemellow, Candy Shade Pouch and Continuum Cog. Four of the launch Pets are Crumble originals. The Pet Gacha unlocks at Quest 39, which requires clearing Stage 1-14 by actively summoning that stage's boss. Every Pet carries two effect layers, and the second is the argument for pulling Pets at all: it applies to every Cookie you own, equipped or not. Scope is derived from the effect text, since the developer publishes no scope field.

      Elemental DMG is not in the Sugar Rune stat pool at all, so it comes from Pets only. That is the one place elements have real mechanical weight in Crumble.

      Cookie portraits are official Devsisters art. Returning franchise Cookies use existing Cookie Run art through the Cookie Run and Cookie Run: Kingdom community wikis; Crumble originals with no franchise equivalent, and the Cookies and Pets added since launch, use their profile image from the game client. Pet art is the franchise Pet sprite set, except the Crumble-original Pets, which use their client profile image too. Every Cookie and Pet in the Database has a portrait.

      What it takes to level a Cookie from 1 to 100, read from the game client: the Cookie EXP each level costs, the Crumble Level your account needs before you can take it, and the stat boost it gives. ATK, DEF and HP all rise by the same percentage of the Cookie's base stat, so one boost column covers all three. Every Cookie uses this same table whatever its rarity.

      Stat boost is the total added to a Cookie's base ATK, DEF and HP at that level, so +2,652.99% at level 100 means 27.53 times its base. It applies before star grade, gear, Sugar Runes and every other source. Level 100 is the cap in the 1.4.002 client: its own guide says so and no level above it exists in the game data. Resetting a Cookie's level returns all the Cookie EXP spent on it.

      The v1.5 update raises the Cookie level cap from 100 to 150. This is what each new level costs in Cookie EXP, the Crumble Level your account needs before you can take it, and the stat boost it gives. From level 101 the Crumble Level requirement climbs five for every Cookie level, so level 150 needs Crumble Level 350.

      Not live yet. This applies with the v1.5 update on 8 Oct 2026. The figures come from a preview of the v1.5 data, not from the live game client, and costs are rounded the way that preview printed them. The Lv.79 to 100 rows of it match the live client exactly on every figure that can be compared.

      Levels 79 to 100 get cheaper

      The same update cuts the Cookie EXP cost of the last 22 levels before 100. Crumble Level requirements and stat boosts for these levels do not change. Level 1 to 100 costs 28.56M in total after the update, down from 98,086,378, a cut of 71%.

      Last updated: July 26, 2026 · Written pre-launch · Rarity board, not a tier list

      Rarity is published. Power is not.

      This page was written before launch, when grades were known for all 75 announced Cookies and not one stat, skill or summon rate had been published. It is kept as written, because the rarity board is still the clearest map of how the crossover roster is organized. Since then the live catalogue became readable, so the numbers now exist: the PvE and PvP boards rank the high-rarity pool and the Database carries the stats and skill text. Any CookieRun: Crumble tier list dated before July 30 is still guesswork.

      Crumble is a crossover roster: 75 confirmed Cookies, 64 pulled from a decade of CookieRun history and 11 built new for this game. The organizing idea is Alternative Cookies, and it does more work than it first appears.

      The five elements

      Fire
      Water
      Grass
      Light
      Dark
      Element advantage, from the in-game Stats reference
      ElementDeals more toBonusTakes more fromIts own penalty
      Fire Grass +15% Water no penalty
      Water Fire +15% Grass no penalty
      Grass Water +15% Fire no penalty
      Light Dark +15% Dark no penalty
      Dark Light +15% Light no penalty
      Printed in-game as Fire ← Water ← Grass ← Fire, Light ↔ Dark; arrows point at the element taking extra damage. The Stats screen shows no multiplier, so the +15% and the zero penalty are ours, from testing rather than off any screen. Attacking into a disadvantage is not punished: the last column is empty by design, not because we could not find the number.

      Fire, Water and Grass run the usual three-way loop. Light and Dark are the odd pair: each has advantage over the other in both directions, so a Light Cookie hits a Dark one harder and takes more back, and neither is a safe answer. An advantage is worth plus 15 percent damage, before your own Elemental DMG stat, which adds on top of it. The half nobody expects is the other side: a disadvantage costs you nothing. The inherent penalty is zero, so a bad matchup deals normal damage rather than reduced damage, and the wheel only ever hands out a bonus. That changes how much it is worth building around. Bringing the countering element is a 15 percent gain, not the difference between working and not working, and you never need to avoid a matchup to dodge a penalty that does not exist. The only way a hit lands for less than normal is if the defender has specifically stacked element resistance, which in the campaign they have not. Ignore charts you see elsewhere for this game: they come from Tower of Adventures, which has six elements including Wind and Earth, or from Kingdom.

      Elements are only half of a Cookie card. A second marker sits beside it, a role or position, and the developer has shown exactly one publicly: the summon screen for Oven Wanderer Cookie reads Fire and Charge at TSSR, tagged Alternative. That single card is the entire public sample of how a Cookie gets classified. Until the full role set is published, build for element coverage, not role theory.

      Alternative Cookies

      Alternative is Crumble's headline roster concept: TSSR reimaginings of classic Cookie Run characters from other timelines. Oven Wanderer Cookie is a parallel-universe GingerBrave. GingerCraven is another one, gone bad. Brightseeker Cookie is an older, wearier GingerBright. The tag appears on the summon screen next to the grade, so it is a real classification, not marketing language.

      The pattern is worth reading before you spend. Every Alternative revealed so far sits at TSSR, and the top grade is almost entirely them. Crumble is not selling nostalgia at the top of the ladder; it is selling the multiverse variant of the character you already like, while the original returns further down.

      The six grades

      Crumble uses C, U, R, SR, SSR, TSSR. This is a new ladder for the franchise, not the Common through Ancient scale CookieRun: Kingdom players know, so Kingdom instincts and rate expectations do not transfer.

      TSSR The top grade. Almost entirely Alternative Cookies, the reimagined classics Crumble is built around, plus Wind Archer as the only straight returning unit at this tier.
      SSR The deepest and widest premium tier. Most of the recognizable later-era franchise cast sits here, plus two costume variants.
      SR Upper mid. Fifteen returning Cookies, mostly the fruit and specialist cast.
      R Lower mid. Notably includes the three Crumble Mercenary Guild leads, so your story protagonists are not premium pulls.
      U Uncommon. Eleven returning Cookies from the classic run era.
      C Common, and the base of the roster. GingerBrave, Strawberry Cookie and Wizard Cookie all return at the bottom tier, a real statement about where Crumble puts franchise nostalgia.
      The official CDN serves grade badge art for R, SSR and TSSR, and the site renders the TSSR badge next to Oven Wanderer Cookie, so those three are first-party. The badge URLs for C, U and SR return 404, so the bottom half of the ladder and every per-Cookie assignment below comes from the community wikis, not the developer. No source explains what the T in TSSR stands for.

      Synergy, Pets & gear reference

      Patch 1.4.002 · Updated October 4, 2026 · How builds actually work under the hood

      Pets attach to the party, not to Cookies

      Pets attach to the PARTY, not to individual Cookies. You equip three from the Lineup menu and only those three apply Companion Effects. A second layer, officially called Passive Effects, applies to every Cookie you own whether the pet is with you or not, so collection breadth pays out independently of selection. Companion Effects come in four scopes: universal, by element, by class, and by Synergy.

      57 Pets: 54 at launch, counted in game as SSR 23, SR 12, R 9, U 6, C 4, and three SSR added since, Chargemellow, Candy Shade Pouch and Continuum Cog. Four of the launch Pets are Crumble originals. The Pet Gacha unlocks at Quest 39, which requires clearing Stage 1-14 by actively summoning that stage's boss.

      Named Pets and their Companion Effects
      PetRarityBest withEffect
      Fluffy Cheese Cat SSR Any Chain team The most build-relevant pet in the game. Ally Chain Synergy +1 and Chain-receiving allies get ATK +5 percent, which makes it effectively a third Chain provider in a game that only has two.
      Holy Baby Drop SSR Universal Ally ATK +10 percent. The best flat team damage Companion Effect published and the safest default in any comp.
      Banana Lion SSR Espresso, Milky Way, Cake Hound Ally Range Synergy +20 percent plus 5 percent ATK to Range recipients. Range is the abundant Synergy and it widens tank radii too.
      Octo Wasabi SSR Poison comp, Milk Pediatrician Ally Duration Synergy +25 percent. Extends buff uptimes and transformation windows, the glue in the poison comp. Passive: Water Cookie ATK +10.

      Hot Doggie SSR Universal Ally Skill AMP +5 percent. Skill Amplification is priced as the strongest stat line in the game, which is why it carries the lowest value at every Sugar Rune tier.

      Eggbeak SSR Charge-heavy squads Charge Ally DMG Reduction +10 percent. One of the class-scoped family with Breadog for Tank evasion and Berry Angrybeak for Ranged accuracy.

      Elemental DMG is not in the Sugar Rune stat pool at all, so it comes from Pets only. That is the one place elements have real mechanical weight in Crumble.

      Gear: the Oven gates slots, not just quality

      Gear comes from the Oven, and your Oven Level decides which equipment slots can physically drop. At Lv.1 only four types exist for you. Each level opens one more until Lv.9, where all twelve are equally likely.

      Lv.1 Sword, Bow, Staff, Helmet 25% each, and 100% Common rarity.
      Lv.2 + Armor 20% each.
      Lv.3 + Shield 16.67% each.
      Lv.4 + Necklace 14.29% each. First Epic at 0.1%.
      Lv.5 + Ring 12.5% each.
      Lv.6 + Brooch 11.11% each.
      Lv.7 + Artifact 10% each.
      Lv.8 + Book 9.09% each.
      Lv.9 to 50 + Food, all 12 8.33% each, flat from here. First Special at 0.08%.

      Sub-stat pools are hard-partitioned by slot, and that partition is the real build constraint.

      Sub-stat pools by gear category
      CategoryPossible sub-statsOdds each
      Sword, Bow, Staff ATK, ACC, CRIT%, CRIT DMG, Skill Amp 20% each, five options
      Helmet, Armor, Shield DEF, HP, EVA, CRIT RES, DMG Reduction 20% each, five options
      Necklace, Ring, Brooch ATK, ACC, CRIT%, CRIT DMG, Skill Amp, Focus, RES, Skill Haste, Mov SPD 11.11% each, nine options
      Artifact, Book, Food DEF, HP, EVA, CRIT RES, DMG Reduction, Focus, RES, Skill Haste, Mov SPD 11.11% each, nine options
      • Your Oven Level is a slot gate, not just a rarity boost. Until Oven Lv.9 there are equipment slots that physically cannot drop for you, so pushing the Oven widens what you can build before it improves what you pull.
      • Get to Oven Lv.2 or Lv.3 immediately for auto-baking. It is the single largest quality-of-life unlock in the game.
      • Sub-stat pools are hard-partitioned by slot, and that is the real build constraint. Weapons are the ONLY source of ATK, CRIT DMG and Skill Amp. Armour is defence only. Accessories are the only source of Skill Haste and Movement Speed.
      • Sub-stat probabilities describe the first sub-stat slot only, and the same sub-stat cannot repeat on one piece.
      • High gear rarity is genuinely far off. Epic first appears at Oven Lv.4 at 0.1%, Special at Lv.9 at 0.08%, Super Epic not until Lv.11 at 0.01%, Unique not until Lv.16. Legendary and Eternal are still 0% at Lv.30.
      • Nothing in the official disclosure or any hands-on source mentions gear SET effects. Do not assume they exist by analogy to other gacha games.

      Plating: free to +9

      Plating is mathematically risk-free through +9. Downgrade risk begins at +10 and destruction risk at +15. There is no compensation for a failure at any level.

      Plating risk bands, from the official probability table
      BandUpgrade chanceRiskWhat to do
      +0 to +9 90% down to 30% None. No downgrade, no break Free progress. Plate every piece you keep to +9 and stop there by default.
      +10 to +14 25% down to 14% Downgrade only, 10% rising to 20% You can lose plate levels but never the item. A reasonable gamble on a good piece.
      +15 to +19 12% down to 2% BREAK, 5% rising to 10% The item can be destroyed outright. Only attempt on a piece you are willing to lose.
      A separate gear enhancement track with five outcomes per attempt: Break, Downgrade, No Change, Upgrade, Super. Full per-level figures are in the Rates and Reroll tab.

      Sugar Runes

      A craftable stat-module system with rarities C through SSR, each with numbered tiers. Movement Speed and Skill Haste apply as flat constants; every other stat applies as a percentage.

      • Skill Amplification carries the LOWEST value at every rarity and tier bar the very bottom one, where it ties, and that is how the game prices it: point for point it is the strongest line in the pool. Do not skip it because the number looks small.
      • What it is NOT is a hundred times better than Crit Damage. Skill Amplification is stored in the same basis points as Crit Damage and Boss Damage, so plus 46.5 percent Skill AMP is the same size of number as plus 40 percent Crit Damage. Writing the formula with Skill AMP over 100 and Crit Damage over 10,000 mixes the on-screen percentage with the raw value, and reading a hundredfold advantage out of that mismatch is a mistake.
      • It is also the one line your team is most likely to have already. Skill Amplification and Skill Haste are the same mechanic from a damage point of view, one raising damage per cast and the other raising casts per second, and buffs are additive inside each. So a squad running a heavy Skill AMP buffer is already deep into diminishing returns on it while nothing at all is buffing Haste. When that is your lineup, gear Haste on the carries and put the Skill Amplification on the buffer, where it multiplies the buff being handed out and so reaches all twelve at once.
      • The best roll is SSR Tier 01 at 0.007663 percent, so chasing a perfect rune is not a plan. Craft for the stat you need and accept the tier.
      • Skill Haste is the RAREST line in the game, not the easiest. Its probability is separate from the thirteen shared stats and roughly double theirs at the tiers it appears on, which is where the opposite reading comes from, but it only appears on four of the twelve tiers: SSR and SR, tiers 01 and 02. Across the whole pool that is 1 in 261, against 1 in 13 for every other stat.
      • Elemental DMG is not in the rune pool at all. It comes from Pets only.

      Stellar Link

      Easily confused with the Lineup grid, and mechanically the opposite of it: this is the twelve-slot board where position provably pays. Star Shards are dealt into slots and the area enclosed by the links between them amplifies the attack, defence and health of every Cookie in the lineup, calculated automatically from the positions with no additional probability roll. The Stellar Link planner under Tools reads your board and tells you what to lock.

      • Placement is random and every arrangement is equally likely. Three active shards give 1,320 possible arrangements; twelve give 479,001,600. Note that the English rate article stops at eleven shards, which is a translation defect: the Korean original runs to twelve.
      • Locking a shard fixes its position while the unlocked ones reshuffle, which the developer confirms. The cap is six locks, and the order is fixed along with the position. Locking is not a convenience feature, it is the only control the system gives you.
      • Do not chase a maximum-area arrangement. At twelve shards a perfect board is one deal in 19,958,400, and on the reset cost ladder the last step alone averages six figures of Stellar Points. Lock what is already good, bank around 85 percent, and stop.
      • Locking exactly one shard is pointless. It costs the same as locking none and changes nothing, because a ring looks identical from every angle.
      • What the bonus is actually worth is published nowhere. The developer confirms it exists and is deterministic, and no source anywhere gives a coefficient.

      Investment priority, in order

      If you do nothing else on this page, do these in this sequence.

      1. Push the main campaign before anything else. Story stages are the only thing that unlocks lineup slots, and each new slot is another live Synergy. You start with 3 slots, get the 5th at Stage 1-8, then 1-27, 3-30, 5-30, 7-30, 9-30, 11-30 and the 12th at 13-30. There is no currency cost, only progress.
      2. Raise your Crumble Level. It is the hard cap on every Cookie's level, and no amount of material fixes a low account level.
      3. Raise Oven Level, and get to Lv.2 or Lv.3 immediately for auto-baking. The Oven is simultaneously your entire gear rarity distribution and the slot unlock track, and you cannot equip all twelve slots until Lv.9.
      4. Own at least one provider for whichever Synergy your best carry receives. Provider scarcity, not rarity, is what gates damage. Wind Archer needs Strawberry Shortcake or Rockstar. A Chain recipient needs Skating Queen, Lime, or the Fluffy Cheese Cat pet.
      5. Level and gear two or three Cookies only, and put attack power first. Both writers who actually played report the progression wall is the boss time limit rather than survival, which makes defensive-first advice wrong.
      6. Plate every piece you keep to +9, which is risk-free, then stop. Plus 10 to plus 14 risks downgrade only. Plus 15 and above can destroy the piece.
      7. Spend spare Coins on Resolve and take the Mercenary Guild perks. Both are cheap account-wide boosts that lift your whole roster at once.
      8. Open Stellar Link when it unlocks. It is a visible power spike and it resets cheaply at low lock counts.
      9. Promote only when you are certain. Cookie levels can be reset at will, so experiment freely with levelling, but promotion is driven by duplicates and is the one irreversible investment.
      10. Pets last. They are a real system with real numbers, but Cookie levels and gear come first. Do claim the Pet Shelter emotion bubbles, which pay free Coins and Crystals and are not mentioned in the tutorial.
      11. Low-rarity Cookies keep their value. Crumble Dungeon deploys your entire collection, and Collections grant permanent account-wide bonuses based on what you have drawn, so breadth pays regardless of rarity.

      The Synergy system behind the builds

      A build in Crumble is not a set of good Cookies. It is a Synergy spine: one Cookie that grants a Synergy plus the Cookies whose kits scale off it. Only 19 of the 76 Cookies grant anything at all, which makes provider access, not rarity, what gates your damage. The game exposes a global Synergy menu with Provider and Recipient tabs, so unlike most launch metas this graph is countable in game, not guessed.

      Counts, not multipliers

      The distinction most coverage gets wrong. Chain, Pierce and Volley are counted in whole STEPS. Range, Duration and Projectile Speed are PERCENTAGES. The evidence is in the pet table: the SSR pet Fluffy Cheese Cat reads "Ally Chain Synergy +1" while its siblings read "Range +20 percent", "Duration +25 percent" and "Projectile Speed +30 percent". So Chain 4 on Twizzly Gummy is four chain steps, not a four-times damage multiplier. What one chain step is worth in damage is not published anywhere, and neither is the magnitude either Cookie Chain provider grants.

      All seven Synergies

      Every kit shows its Synergy-scaled terms on the card, and the game exposes a global Synergy menu with Provider and Recipient tabs, so unlike most launch metas the whole graph is countable in game. Only 19 of the 76 Cookies grant anything, the real scarcity here. Provider access, not rarity, gates your damage. Of the seven Cookies added since launch only Pinot Noir Cookie grants one, Rapid Fire. Cool Mint Cookie did not move that number when she arrived: she takes Volley and Duration and supplies neither, which is the majority position on this roster rather than a knock on her.

      Range

      Abundant Percentage

      Range is increased.

      Providers 4
      Recipients 18

      The most buildable Synergy, and it widens tank damage radii as a side effect, so it also buffs your front line. Macaron Cookie provides it at SR, the budget enabler for Espresso and Milky Way.

      Duration

      Healthy Percentage

      Skill duration increases.

      Providers 3
      Recipients 15

      Extends buff uptimes and transformation windows. Coffee and Cheerleader both provide it at Uncommon rarity, so it is cheap to switch on.

      Rapid Fire

      Skills activate more times in succession.

      Providers 2

      Two providers for twelve recipients. Grapevine, a free starter, is one of the two, which is what makes the early free-roster comp work.

      Volley

      Shots fired simultaneously increase.

      Providers 3
      Recipients 10

      Cheesecake provides it at R rarity, the cheapest route to accelerating Scorpion's poison stacking.

      The narrowest of the percentage Synergies. Pomegranate provides it at 75 percent alongside its team Skill AMP buff.

      Pierce

      Providers 2

      Strawberry Shortcake at SSR and Rockstar at SR. In the high-rarity pool it is effectively a single pair with Wind Archer, which is why the Pierce lock below is a hard dependency, not a preference.

      Chain

      Providers 2

      The scarcest Synergy and the hardest to supply: Skating Queen at SSR and Lime at SR are the only two Cookie providers, though the SSR pet Fluffy Cheese Cat acts as a third. Running a Chain recipient without a provider wastes most of its kit.

      Provider cheat sheet

      Only 19 of 76 Cookies grant a Synergy. Provider access, not rarity, gates your damage, and several providers are available far below SSR. If you own a strong carry with no provider for its Synergy, most of its kit is switched off.

      Cheapest and best provider for each Synergy
      SynergyBudget providerPremium providerNotes
      Chain Lime Cookie (SR) Skating Queen Cookie (SSR) The SSR pet Fluffy Cheese Cat reads Ally Chain Synergy +1, which acts as a third provider.
      Pierce Rockstar Cookie (SR) Strawberry Shortcake Cookie (SSR) Rockstar is the budget route to switching on Wind Archer.
      Range Macaron Cookie (SR), Knight Cookie (U) Cream Soda and Toothpaste both grant 50 percent Knight both grants and receives Range, so it buffs itself.
      Rapid Fire Grapevine Cookie (R), Orange Cookie (SR) None in the high-rarity pool Grapevine is a free starter, which is what makes the early free-roster comp function.
      Volley Cheesecake Cookie (R), Tiger Lily Cookie (SR) Herb Cookie (SR) The cheapest way to accelerate Scorpion poison stacking.
      Duration Coffee Cookie (U), Cheerleader Cookie (U) Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician (SSR) Two Uncommon providers make Duration the cheapest Synergy to enable.
      Projectile Speed Alchemist Cookie (R) Pomegranate Cookie (SSR) at 75 percent

      Do not write off the low rarities. Lime at SR is one of only two Chain providers in the entire game. Herb at SR is reported appearing even in SSR teams because it is the best healer in its band. Skater Cookie at Common is the only Common-rarity Chain recipient. Crumble Dungeon deploys your entire collection and Collections grant permanent account-wide bonuses, so roster breadth has standing value regardless of tier.

      Team comps

      These are Synergy spines, not twelve-slot lineups, because the remaining slots should go to whatever you actually pulled and you will not have twelve slots for a long time anyway. Build the spine first, then fill. The in-game Synergy menu lists Providers and Recipients, so you can check your own bench against the graph above in about a minute.

      Corroborated

      Pierce lock

      Horde clear and stage push

      Cookies2

      Core: Both halves. Neither functions as intended without the other. In the high-rarity pool Pierce has exactly one provider and one recipient. Two sources reached this from opposite directions, the kit-reader from the in-game Synergy menu and a hands-on writer who put it as an imperative. Rockstar Cookie at SR is the budget substitute for Shortcake. This is a hard dependency, not a preference.

      Corroborated

      Chain party

      Arena and general-purpose core

      Cookies4

      Core: One Chain provider. There are only two in the roster: Skating Queen at SSR and Lime at SR. The strongest signal in the dataset, because a kit-reader and a player converged on the same team from opposite methods. Chain runs 2 providers against 5 recipients and carries the largest terms in the game: four chain steps on Twizzly Gummy, three on Oven Wanderer, two on Vampire. Note those are step counts, not damage multipliers, and what a step is worth is unpublished.

      Single source

      Universal glue

      Slot-agnostic core, not a full comp

      Cookies4

      Core: Pomegranate and Dark Choco, both of which multiply whatever else you bring. None of these four care how many enemies are on screen or which mode you are running. Between them: plus 46.5 percent team Skill AMP at 90 percent uptime, ATK plus 6 percent stacking ten times, minus 25 percent enemy DEF at full stacks, and CRIT DMG plus 40 percent. That is four separate stat lines rather than four servings of one, which is the case for fielding them together, though the developer does not publish how Skill AMP combines with ATK. Two of the four are free.

      Single source

      Early free-roster push

      Early campaign, five unlocked slots, no pulls required

      Cookies5

      Core: A Rapid Fire provider. Grapevine is the accessible one. Built by a hands-on writer around what every account actually owns, and mechanically justified rather than asserted. Dark Cherry is free and arrives with a duplicate, and only works as damage once Rapid Fire is switched on. Grapevine and Orange are the only two Rapid Fire providers you will see early. Knight supplies Range to itself and the line.

      Single source

      Poison stack

      Mid to late progression for accounts that never landed a TSSR

      Cookies10

      Core: Scorpion as the carry, a Volley provider to accelerate poison application, a Duration provider to hold the buffs up. The only published mid-game comp written by someone with the game open, and internally coherent: Volley raises how many skills fire simultaneously, which speeds Scorpion's poison stacking, while Duration extends the buff windows so the loop sustains. Worth knowing that Scorpion itself is still unranked on the board above, though not for the reason this comp was written with: the missing figure was identified as DoT Chance, 100 percent at 5 stars, so every application lands a stack, and what is unresolved now is whether a fresh application refreshes the stacks already on the target. Duration is also not the only lever on the ramp, because the Stats screen defines Skill Haste as reducing skill cooldown, which shortens the 4.25 seconds between applications while Duration lengthens the 5 seconds each stack lasts.

      Single source

      Boss swap

      Boss timers and single-target damage

      Cookies7

      Core: Vampire plus a Chain provider, because Vampire's Chain-scaled hits all land on the same target. Assembled from one source's boss-damage board rather than published anywhere as a comp, and flagged as such. The structural point is well supported: against a single target area coverage stops paying and concentration takes over. Twizzly Gummy and the wide-area tanks are deliberately absent.

      Corroborated

      Crumble Dungeon

      Not a twelve-slot problem at all

      Cookies1

      Core: Roster breadth plus account-wide multipliers. Officially described as sending every Cookie in your collection into one battle against the Holy Golden Drop, ranked on total damage, and independently confirmed by a Korean hands-on preview. There is no best-in-slot Crumble Dungeon comp. The levers are pet Passive Effects, which apply to every Cookie you own whether equipped or not, and Collection bonuses. This is the strongest argument for keeping a broad collection regardless of rarity.

      Cookie and Pet art: Devsisters. Every portrait was checked against that Cookie's in-game catalogue card before publishing. Returning franchise Cookies and Pets use existing Cookie Run and Cookie Run: Kingdom community-wiki art; Crumble originals with no franchise equivalent, and the Cookies and Pets added since launch, use their profile image from the game client.

      Upcoming

      Read straight from the CookieRun: Crumble game client, version 1.4.002 (data set 3 Oct 2026, checked 4 Oct 2026). None of this is announced. It is what the client already carries ahead of release, so names, numbers and timing can change before anything ships. Anything the client does not hold is marked as missing rather than guessed. A few figures come from a preview of the v1.5 data, the update dated 8 Oct 2026, which EOG has seen but not read first-hand: those sit under their own heading on the card.

      Mode In the client

      Crumb Clash

      Art from the game client

      A season-based PvP mode built around a Base you grow, Bear Jellies you hire, and resources you take from Hunts, Treasure Chests, Outposts and other players’ Bases. The live game already shows its tab with a COMING SOON popup; its gameplay tables are not in this build.

      Unlocks
      After Quest 100: clear Stage 3-30
      Team
      6 Cookies plus your hired Bear Jellies
      Base
      20 levels, from Abandoned Crate to Giant Bear Jelly Tower; each level raises the cap of the other buildings
      Buildings
      Base, Hiring Center (Bear Jellies), Tech Lab (90 research nodes), Security Office (defence lineup)
      Bear Jellies
      15 units across Tank, Charge and Ranged, 10 levels each
      Resources
      Wood and Jellybeans (common), Iron (premium), Money (rare), Honor (ranking)
      Ranks
      29 tiers, Chocolate 2 up to Grandmaster 1
      Seasons
      Ten season names exist; no dates in this build

      Exploration zones

      • Treasure Chests (Normal, Advanced, Premium; daily cap)
      • Hunts against 9 targets, harder at higher Hunt level
      • Outposts that produce resources once held: 5 kinds, 5 grades each
      • Bases: raid other players and take their resources, with Revenge battles

      Rules worth knowing

      • Cookies that win an Outpost become its defenders and cannot be swapped while you hold it
      • Up to 50% of injured Bear Jellies return
      • Daily ranking rewards at midnight GMT+9; season rewards when the season ends

      Rewards named

      • Crumb Clash #1 frames
      • Master, Elite Master and Grandmaster icons
      • Titles for first reaching Diamond, Master, Elite Master and Grandmaster, and for 1,000 plays

      Some write-ups call it Crumble Clash; the game’s English name is Crumb Clash.

      Last updated: August 1, 2026 · Live since July 30 · Sourced from official material and launch-week play

      Written by people playing it

      CookieRun: Crumble went live July 30, 2026 and EOG has played since launch day. This guide started from the official material, store listings and official screenshots, and is now checked against the live game. Where the developer publishes a name but not a number, it says so rather than filling the gap. Nothing here is guessed, and where a figure came from community testing rather than from the developer, the page names the difference.

      CookieRun: Crumble is a Korean idle game out of Seoul. You assemble a squad of up to twelve Cookies, send it at a stage, and it fights on its own: moving, attacking, and firing skills without input. Your gameplay is everything around the fight: who is in the squad, its element mix, attached Pets, which of the five lineup presets you load, and how often you collect. The developer calls it hands-off, and means it.

      The loop

      1. Push stages until you stall. Stages run in chapter-dash-stage format and go deep; the official screenshots show stage 84-24, so the ladder is long. Your squad auto-repeats the highest stage it can hold.
      2. Your stage sets your income. Idle newcomers miss this. Auto Hunt pays based on the stage you are parked on, and the reward screen advertises the better rate waiting at the next one. Progress is not bragging rights, it is your earn rate.
      3. Collect, invest, repeat. Claim the Auto Hunt bank, pour it into levels, stars, and Pets, then push one more stage to raise the rate again.
      4. Spend the overflow on the side modes. Crumble Dungeon, Plaque Tower, The Arena, and Crumb Clash each want a squad tuned differently from your stage-pusher. That is what the five presets exist for.

      Auto Hunt is the whole economy

      Offline earnings, called Auto Hunt Rewards, stop accruing at a cap that is not a fixed number and not tied to your stage. 8 hours is the base on a new account, and it grows with what you build and buy.

      The cap rises with your Sweet Blessing level, Gnome Laboratory upgrades, and purchased packs. Stage clears raise reward quantity, not duration. A new account has only 8 hours of slack, so read your own panel rather than trusting a quoted figure.

      The rule is the same: a daily player never touches the ceiling, a weekend away is a real loss, and logging in twice a day buys nothing over once. All that matters is never letting a single gap exceed your cap.

      The developer has not published Auto Hunt rates for launch-window stages, and the 105K Coins per minute in the screenshots is a stage 84-24 figure, nothing like your first week.

      Four growth tracks

      Level. Capped by your account Crumble Level, not a fixed number, so raising Crumble Level lifts every Cookie's ceiling. Levels reset at will, so you can experiment freely.

      Promotion. A separate rank track; the store sells a five-stage Cookie Promotion Pass against it, which marks it a meaningful wall, not a formality.

      Gear. Not farmed. You collect Lucky Dough and a Sugar Gnome rolls equipment out of an oven for you, making gear a third randomized draw behind Cookies and Pets.

      Pets. Their own summon currency and power layer. The developer splits Pet effects into a Companion Effect, tied to the paired Cookie, and a separate Passive Effect.

      Above all of it sits the grade a Cookie was born at: C, U, R, SR, SSR, TSSR. Grades are known for all 75 confirmed Cookies. What a grade changes beyond stat ceilings, how stars are raised, and whether duplicates feed the star track are all unpublished.

      Systems reference: every number actually published
      Squad size 12 A 2 by 6 hex grid of Cookie slots. They deploy into an open arena and move, attack and fire skills on their own. Whether front vs back row matters mechanically is undocumented.
      Lineup presets 5 Five saved lineups, switched from tabs above the roster and from a selector on the battle HUD, so you can swap squads from the field.
      Battle speed x0.5 to x2 Four speed settings. With the preset selector and a Summon Boss button plus an Auto Summon Reservation toggle, that is the complete set of confirmed in-combat inputs.
      Elements 5 Fire, Water, Grass, Light, and Dark. From the element table in the official pre-registration payload, so first-party.
      Rarity grades 6 C, U, R, SR, SSR, TSSR. The official CDN serves grade badges for R, SSR and TSSR only; the other three come from the community wikis.
      Roster 70 Sixty-nine Cookies were obtainable day one, against 75 documented before launch, and Cool Mint Cookie made seventy on August 13. The 23 high-rarity units are 2 TSSR and 21 SSR, the complete top of the pool.
      Classes 4 Charge, Ranged, Tank and Support. Stats are class templates rather than per-Cookie values, so the in-game Power number is not a ranking signal.
      Synergies 7 Range, Duration, Rapid Fire, Volley, Projectile Speed, Pierce and Chain. Only 19 of the 76 Cookies grant one, so provider access is the real constraint on damage.
      Auto Hunt cap 8h and up Not a fixed number and not stage-gated. Every account starts at 8 hours; the cap then rises with Sweet Blessing level, Gnome Laboratory upgrades, and purchased packs. Clearing stages raises the reward rate, not the hours. Read your own cap off the Auto Hunt Rewards panel.
      Cookie level cap Crumble Level A Cookie's maximum level is gated by your account Crumble Level, not a fixed number, so raising Crumble Level lifts the ceiling on every Cookie. Levels reset at will, so levelling is a safe experiment.
      Growth axes 4 Level and stars, promotion, gear, and Pets. Gear comes from an oven-style automatic draw rather than manual farming.
      Stamina system None visible No stamina meter, fatigue bar, or energy counter appears in any of the ten official store screenshots. The field HUD carries only Coins and Crystals. A verified absence in published material, not a confirmed design decision.
      Visible IAP band $0.99 to $11.99 Across the top ten purchases Apple displays. Apple caps that list at ten, so this is the top of what is visible, not a ceiling.
      Languages 5 English, Japanese, Korean, Thai, and Chinese. No European languages at launch, so global here means Asia-first with an English catch-all.

      Your first session

      • Bind your account before anything else. The store listing warns explicitly: play as a guest and your data is gone if you uninstall. Link it first, then play.
      • Claim the pre-registration mail. Roughly 500 summon items plus 1,000 Crystals and 10,000 Coins are waiting. They expire August 29 at 11:59 PM GMT+9.
      • Push stages before you optimize anything. Your stage sets your Auto Hunt rate, so early progress compounds harder than any squad tuning at level 10.
      • Read your Auto Hunt cap off the rewards panel, then never exceed it. It is not fixed: you start at 8 hours and raise it with Sweet Blessing, Gnome Laboratory upgrades and packs, never by clearing stages. Set a reminder if your schedule is uneven. This is the highest-value habit in the game.

      Reroll answer · Patch 1.0 · Rates transcribed verbatim from the official disclosure

      Rates are a function of Gacha Level

      Every Cookie and Pet gacha rate is a function of GACHA LEVEL, not a fixed number. At Gacha Lv.1 the Premium Cookie pool is 82.00% Common and 18.00% Uncommon, with 0.0000% chance of R, SR, SSR or TSSR. SSR is impossible until Lv.4. TSSR is impossible until Lv.6, and even at Lv.10 it is 0.0500%, one in two thousand. A brand-new account cannot pull a high-rarity Cookie at all.

      Should you reroll? No.

      Do not reroll. A brand-new account sits at Gacha Lv.1, where the Premium Cookie pool is 82% Common, 18% Uncommon, and 0.0000% everything else. There is no lucky high-rarity start to chase, so the premise of a reroll collapses before it begins.

      Where to go next

      Ready to build? Head to Tier List & Builds for the PvE and PvP boards and the exact lineups our top-ranked players field.

      Not sure what to field? Tools has Mixture, which takes the Cookies you actually own and returns the lineup that switches on the most Synergy for your carry. Alongside it: the Stellar Link planner, a Draw simulator running the official rates, the Stage Power Chart, and a Build Maker to share a squad.

      Wondering if a Cookie is worth levelling? Simulators has the Damage Lab, which ranks all 76 at your own gear rather than at somebody else's, and the Dungeon Sim, which plays out a Crumble Dungeon run slot by slot so you can see who arrives too late to matter.
